sets.relationshipLabel: the worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A tailor is defined by the tape measure just as a seamstress is defined by the sewing machine — each pair names a craftsperson and the instrument that does their signature work.

sets.relationshipLabel: two ends of a garment's vertical axis, top to bottom
sets.explanation: Collar-to-waistband and shoulder-to-cuff each span a garment from its highest point to its lowest, the same top-to-bottom stretch measured on two different parts.

sets.relationshipLabel: the thing that stops a specific flaw from occurring
sets.explanation: A thimble exists to stop the prick of a needle, and selvage exists to stop the fraying of cut fabric — each item is built specifically to prevent the flaw named beside it.

sets.relationshipLabel: the real form and the made image used to plan or fit it
sets.explanation: A dress form stands in for the torso and a sketch stands in for the jacket — both are made images used to plan or fit the real thing they represent, one sculpted, one drawn.
